sentences.en: Our story begins in 1835, or maybe 1935, or maybe the last time you woke up with a hangover from the wine at the gas station, you know, Franzia's evil cousin,
sentences.zh: 我们的故事始于1835年，或许是1935年，又或许是你上一次宿醉醒来的时候，那酒来自加油站，你知道的，就是弗兰齐亚（Franzia）的邪恶表亲，

sentences.en: and you asked yourself, is this normal?
sentences.zh: 你问自己，这正常吗？

sentences.en: Is it normal to feel this way?
sentences.zh: 这种感觉正常吗？

sentences.en: Let's work our way backwards.
sentences.zh: 让我们倒叙来看。

sentences.en: Today on the show, we have the incredible comedian, writer, and podcaster, Jamie Loftus.
sentences.zh: 今天节目请到了杰出的喜剧演员、作家兼播客主持人杰米·洛夫图斯（Jamie Loftus）。

sentences.en: I can't remember a time in my life when I didn't know what Alcoholics Anonymous was.
sentences.zh: 我不记得我人生中有哪段时间不知道“匿名戒酒互助会”（AA）是什么。

sentences.en: We talked about it at home like a friend that lived in the same neighborhood.
sentences.zh: 我们在家里谈论它，就像谈论一位住在同一个街区的邻居朋友。

sentences.en: Dad was going to a meeting tonight, so wait outside or in the hallway of the high school until it's over.
sentences.zh: 爸爸今晚要去开会，所以我就在外面或者高中的走廊里等着，直到会议结束。

sentences.en: Then walk through the cloud of cigarette smoke and friendly conversation when the AA hour, and it was always exactly an hour, was up.
sentences.zh: 然后，当AA的会议时间——总是准时一小时——结束后，我穿过那片烟雾缭绕和友好交谈的人群。

sentences.en: I can count on one hand, for my entire childhood, a time where a close family member drank in front of the kids,
sentences.zh: 整个童年时期，我一只手就能数出家里有亲近的长辈当着孩子的面喝酒的次数，

sentences.en: even though pictures from before I was born were so full of alcohol that you couldn't always make out the ruddy-faced younger versions of my dad, aunts, and uncles.
sentences.zh: 尽管我出生前的照片里到处都是酒，以至于你有时都认不出照片里那些面色红润、年轻版的爸爸、阿姨和叔叔们。

sentences.en: Later, when I went to dad for advice, he could rarely avoid just saying it directly.
sentences.zh: 后来，当我向爸爸寻求建议时，他很少能避免直接说出来。

sentences.en: Take things one day at a time.
sentences.zh: 过好每一天。

sentences.en: Find the serenity to accept the things I could not change, the courage to change the things I could,
sentences.zh: 寻找内心的平静，去接受我无法改变的事情；拥有勇气，去改变我能改变的事情；

sentences.en: and, say it with me now, the wisdom to know the difference.
sentences.zh: 还有，跟我一起说，拥有智慧去分辨这两者。

sentences.en: These meetings were important, I thought.
sentences.zh: 我想，这些会议很重要。

sentences.en: They'd protect our family from whatever had happened.
sentences.zh: 它们能保护我们的家庭免受过去发生的一切的影响。

sentences.en: And they and my mom's patients would keep us all together from an evil I had never seen or tasted.
sentences.zh: 它们和我妈妈的病人们会让我们团结在一起，抵御一种我从未见过或尝过的邪恶。

sentences.en: Even though I wasn't totally sure what an Alcoholics Anonymous meeting was.
sentences.zh: 尽管我并不完全确定匿名戒酒互助会会议到底是什么。

sentences.en: Two weeks before my dad died in 2024, he hit an incredible marker.
sentences.zh: 在我爸爸2024年去世前两周，他达成了一个了不起的里程碑。

sentences.en: 30 years sober from alcohol.
sentences.zh: 戒酒30年。

sentences.en: The first five years or so spent going to AA meetings every single day.
sentences.zh: 最初的五年左右，他每天都去参加AA会议。

sentences.en: The influence AA had on my family was gigantic in ways I was told about and ways it would take me years to understand.
sentences.zh: AA对我家庭的影响是巨大的，有些是我被告知的，有些则需要我花上几年时间去理解。

sentences.en: Influencing not just how my family behaved, but how we thought.
sentences.zh: 它不仅影响了我家人的行为方式，还影响了我们的思维方式。

sentences.en: But as a kid, the only tactile evidence I had that AA existed was something I was kind of obsessed with.
sentences.zh: 但作为一个孩子，我所拥有的关于AA存在的唯一实物证据，是我有点痴迷的东西。

sentences.en: This little album where dad kept all his sobriety chips.
sentences.zh: 这本小相册，爸爸把他的戒酒纪念币都放在里面。

sentences.en: He, along with most AA members, started accruing these at his first meeting,
sentences.zh: 他和大多数AA成员一样，从第一次参加会议就开始积攒这些纪念币，

sentences.en: right after he got out of the three days of detox that his health insurance covered.
sentences.zh: 就在他结束了医疗保险覆盖的三天排毒治疗之后。

sentences.en: You collect sobriety chips the fastest in your first year clean.
sentences.zh: 在戒酒的第一年，你收集纪念币的速度最快。

sentences.en: At 24 hours, 30 days, 60 days, 90 days, all the way up to a year in most groups, and often annually after that.
sentences.zh: 大多数小组会在24小时、30天、60天、90天时发放，一直到一年，之后通常每年发放一次。

sentences.en: My dad was never precious about belongings, but these chips were really important to him.
sentences.zh: 我爸爸从不把身外之物看得太重，但这些纪念币对他来说真的很重要。

sentences.en: The rare things that my brother and I were not allowed to touch.
sentences.zh: 这是我和哥哥被禁止触碰的少数几样东西之一。

sentences.en: They meant something.
sentences.zh: 它们意义非凡。

sentences.en: And if the way everyone else acted was an indicator,
sentences.zh: 如果其他人的行为方式可以作为指标的话，

sentences.en: it was mom's support and dad's commitment to Alcoholics Anonymous that was the reason that I had a relationship with him at all.
sentences.zh: 正是妈妈的支持和爸爸对匿名戒酒互助会的承诺，才让我得以与他建立起联系。

sentences.en: Fast forward to this year, my dad was gone, I was in my 30s, and I had to face the fact that I'd developed a shaky relationship with alcohol.
sentences.zh: 快进到今年，爸爸去世了，我三十多岁了，我不得不面对一个事实：我和酒精的关系变得岌岌可危。

sentences.en: And I found myself on a work trip to Iowa with one of those little white plastic chips in my hand.
sentences.zh: 我发现自己在去爱荷华州出差的路上，手里拿着那枚白色的小塑料币。

sentences.en: One of my own.
sentences.zh: 属于我自己的那一枚。

sentences.en: One even flimsier than the 24-hour chip in dad's album.
sentences.zh: 甚至比爸爸相册里那枚24小时纪念币还要单薄。

sentences.en: Our stories were really different.
sentences.zh: 我们的故事截然不同。

sentences.en: I hadn't hit bottom.
sentences.zh: 我还没有跌入谷底。

sentences.en: There was no relationship with a spouse or a child on the line.
sentences.zh: 没有配偶或孩子的关系受到威胁。

sentences.en: I just knew I had to make a change.
sentences.zh: 我只是知道我必须做出改变。

sentences.en: And even though I'm far from alone there, there's around 30 million Americans that have some degree of alcohol use disorder.
sentences.zh: 尽管我远非孤身一人，大约有3000万美国人患有不同程度的酒精使用障碍。

sentences.en: I felt pretty embarrassed about it.
sentences.zh: 我对此感到非常尴尬。

sentences.en: And when I started looking into how that little white chip got there, I found a story that was so profoundly and infuriatingly American.
sentences.zh: 当我开始研究那枚白色小纪念币的由来时，我发现了一个如此深刻且令人愤怒的美国故事。

sentences.en: It's the kind of story that really makes you want to take a drink.
sentences.zh: 这是一个真正让你想喝上一杯的故事。

sentences.en: Imbued in this little chip is a hidden history that contains centuries of Americans' relationship to morality, to religion, and even to gender, to identity.
sentences.zh: 这枚小小的纪念币中蕴含着一段隐藏的历史，包含了几个世纪以来美国人与道德、宗教、甚至性别和身份的关系。

sentences.en: That's a pretty potent piece of plastic.
sentences.zh: 那真是一块充满力量的塑料片。

sentences.en: From 99% Invisible and BBC Studios, this is a history of the United States in 100 Objects.
sentences.zh: 来自《99%无形》（99% Invisible）和BBC工作室，这是《100件物品中的美国史》。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯（Roman Mars）。

sentences.en: Today, the Alcoholics Anonymous sobriety chip.
sentences.zh: 今天的主题是：匿名戒酒互助会的戒酒纪念币。

sentences.en: Alcoholics Anonymous wasn't born in a void in 1935.
sentences.zh: 匿名戒酒互助会并非在1935年凭空诞生。

sentences.en: It was a response to a massive, mostly failed political movement that proved once and for all that morality is impossible to legislate.
sentences.zh: 它是对一场大规模且基本失败的政治运动的回应，这场运动一劳永逸地证明了道德是不可能通过立法来强制执行的。

sentences.en: Luckily, American legislators have since learned not to do that, a fact you might agree with if you cannot read, hear, or see.
sentences.zh: 幸运的是，美国立法者们此后学会了不再那样做，如果你不识字、听不见或看不见，你可能会同意这一事实。

sentences.en: I'm talking about American Prohibition, which ran from 1920 to 1933, about a year and a half before the first AA meetings took place.
sentences.zh: 我说的是美国的禁酒令，从1920年持续到1933年，大约在第一次AA会议召开前一年半。

sentences.en: Now, I didn't learn about Prohibition in school, in spite of hearing a lot about the history taking place around it.
sentences.zh: 虽然我听过很多关于禁酒令背景的历史，但在学校里我并没有学过这段历史。

sentences.en: Women's suffrage passes the same year as Prohibition, and the issue hovers around rapid industrialization, World War I, the Great Depression,
sentences.zh: 妇女选举权与禁酒令在同一年通过，这个问题围绕着快速工业化、第一次世界大战、大萧条，

sentences.en: and a massive early 20th century wave of immigration from Europe to the United States.
sentences.zh: 以及20世纪初从欧洲到美国的大规模移民潮。

sentences.en: But today, with the exception of my close personal friend Ken Burns' docuseries on the topic, Prohibition has been boiled culturally down to two images.
sentences.zh: 但今天，除了我私交甚笃的朋友肯·伯恩斯（Ken Burns）关于该主题的纪录片系列外，禁酒令在文化上已被简化为两个形象。

sentences.en: The gangster and the flapper.
sentences.zh: 黑帮分子和摩登女郎。

sentences.en: The gangster.
sentences.zh: 黑帮分子。

sentences.en: Usually Al Capone, or a thinly veiled version of him, is violent, powerful, and endlessly charismatic, appearing everywhere from Scarface to The Godfather to Tintin.
sentences.zh: 通常是阿尔·卡彭（Al Capone），或者是以他为原型的角色，暴力、强大且极具魅力，从《疤面煞星》到《教父》再到《丁丁历险记》，到处都有他们的身影。

sentences.en: The flapper is his counterpart, a liberated woman of the jazz age.
sentences.zh: 摩登女郎是他的对应形象，爵士时代的解放女性。

sentences.en: Think gentlemen-preferred blondes and Daisy Buchanans, partying in these dank, glamorous speakeasies, drinking martinis, and completely free of the responsibilities of the home.
sentences.zh: 想想《绅士爱美人》里的金发女郎和黛西·布坎南，在那些阴暗迷人的地下酒吧里狂欢，喝着马提尼，完全摆脱了家庭责任。

sentences.en: But there's so much more to this time, when the law of the land constitutionally banned production, import, transport, or sale of alcoholic beverages.
sentences.zh: 但那个时代远不止于此，当时国家的法律在宪法层面禁止了酒精饮料的生产、进口、运输或销售。

sentences.en: Passed through the 18th Amendment and enforced by the cruel and inefficient Volstead Act, it's weird that we don't talk about Prohibition more often.
sentences.zh: 通过第18修正案并由残酷且低效的《沃尔斯泰德法案》（Volstead Act）强制执行，奇怪的是我们竟然不常谈论禁酒令。

sentences.en: After all, it's the only constitutional amendment that's been repealed.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，它是唯一被废除的宪法修正案。

sentences.en: Ever.
sentences.zh: 有史以来唯一一个。

sentences.en: So why does it get lost in the shuffle?
sentences.zh: 那么为什么它会被遗忘呢？

sentences.en: Well, I think it's partially because everybody thinks they know everything about it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为部分原因是每个人都觉得自己对它了如指掌。

sentences.en: You know, everyone just thinks, oh, we've heard all those gangster stories a million times and we don't want to listen to them anymore.
sentences.zh: 你知道，大家只是觉得，哦，那些黑帮故事我们都听过一百万遍了，不想再听了。

sentences.en: This is Gioia Diliberto, author of Firebrands, the untold story of four women who made an unmade Prohibition, a book that tackles this question head on.
sentences.zh: 这是乔亚·迪利伯托（Gioia Diliberto），《火种》（Firebrands）的作者，讲述了四位女性制造并终结禁酒令的未公开故事，这本书正面探讨了这个问题。

sentences.en: She and most historians are sure about one thing.
sentences.zh: 她和大多数历史学家都确定一件事。

sentences.en: Prohibition was a crummy idea and it didn't work.
sentences.zh: 禁酒令是个烂主意，而且根本行不通。

sentences.en: I mean, it failed because it was just a bad idea from the get go.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，它失败了，因为它从一开始就是个坏主意。

sentences.en: You know, I mean, it's incredible that a constitutional amendment was passed instituting Prohibition.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我的意思是，通过一项宪法修正案来实施禁酒令真是令人难以置信。

sentences.en: The 18th Amendment went into effect in 1920, but this was after close to a century of temperance activism.
sentences.zh: 第18修正案于1920年生效，但这是在近一个世纪的节制运动之后。

sentences.en: And while Prohibition fails for a million reasons we can explore, what's true is that prior to Prohibition, Americans drank much more alcohol.
sentences.zh: 虽然禁酒令因我们可以探讨的一百万个原因而失败，但事实是，在禁酒令之前，美国人喝的酒要多得多。

sentences.en: In 1830, the average person drank three times more than they did by the 2010s, the equivalent of 88 bottles of whiskey a year.
sentences.zh: 1830年，人均饮酒量是2010年代的三倍，相当于每年88瓶威士忌。

sentences.en: And the culture around alcohol was marketed almost exclusively to men.
sentences.zh: 而且围绕酒精的文化几乎完全是针对男性营销的。

sentences.en: Saloons became the social center of communities in the back half of the 1800s.
sentences.zh: 在19世纪后半叶，酒吧成为了社区的社交中心。

sentences.en: There were around 250,000 of them in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 在鼎盛时期，美国大约有25万家酒吧，

sentences.en: at their peak and were a place where men could get a hot lunch, connect with translators and job prospects, cast their ballots, meet their unions, and of course,
sentences.zh: 它们是男人们可以吃热午餐、联系翻译和工作机会、投票、会见工会成员的地方，当然，

sentences.en: get blackout drunk on the alcohol of whichever brewery owned the joint.
sentences.zh: 还可以喝着拥有这家店的酿酒厂提供的酒，喝到不省人事。

sentences.en: And with the popularity of saloons came the country's first temperance group, the Washingtonian Society, established in Baltimore in 1840.
sentences.zh: 随着酒吧的流行，全国第一个节制团体——华盛顿协会（Washingtonian Society）于1840年在巴尔的摩成立。

sentences.en: The Washingtonians' philosophy was pretty close to what A.A.
sentences.zh: 华盛顿协会的理念与AA在近一个世纪后所宣扬的非常接近。

sentences.en: would be saying nearly a century later.
sentences.zh: 它由有饮酒问题的男性组成，在小组会议中分享他们的经历，并承诺戒酒。

sentences.en: It was composed of men with drinking problems, sharing their experiences in a group meeting, and pledging abstinence.
sentences.zh: 这是作家T.S.亚瑟（T.S. Arthur）对该团体的描述。

sentences.en: Here's writer T.S.
sentences.zh: 他们聚集在这个城市的一家酒馆里，六个年事已高的人，长期以来一直是无可救药的酒鬼，

sentences.en: Arthur on the group.
sentences.zh: 或者至少是如此沉溺于烈酒的爱。

sentences.en: They were assembled in a drinking house in this city, six men, well-advanced in years, who had for a long time been confirmed drunkards,
sentences.zh: 他们是偶然相遇的，但每个人的心中都有一种对自身被奴役和悲惨处境的悲伤，一种想要摆脱它的强烈愿望，却又有一种痛苦的、

sentences.en: or at least so wedded to the love of strong drink.
sentences.zh: 绝望的软弱感。

sentences.en: They had met accidentally, but in the mind of each there was a feeling of sorrow for his enslaved and wretched condition, a strong desire to rise out of it, yet a painful,
sentences.zh: 华盛顿协会拥有数万名成员。

sentences.en: hopeless sense of weakness.
sentences.zh: 它在当时非常受欢迎，以至于亚伯拉罕·林肯在1842年还对他们发表过演讲。

sentences.en: The Washingtonians counted tens of thousands of men as members.
sentences.zh: 但几十年后，该团体的受欢迎程度下降了。

sentences.en: It was so popular at the time that Abe Lincoln gave a speech to them in 1842.
sentences.zh: 据推测，他们失败的罪魁祸首是华盛顿协会卷入了无关的进步政治事业。

sentences.en: But after a few decades, the group's popularity waned.
sentences.zh: 记住这一点，因为AA在这一方面做出了非常不同的决定。

sentences.en: The culprit for their failure, it's been speculated, was the Washingtonians' entanglement in unrelated progressive political causes.
sentences.zh: 那些进步事业恰好是废奴运动、女权运动和更大规模的节制运动。

sentences.en: And put a pin in that because A.A.
sentences.zh: 这些事业在整个19世纪到20世纪不断重叠。

sentences.en: makes a very different decision in that department.
sentences.zh: 弗雷德里克·道格拉斯（Frederick Douglass）是一位著名的禁酒主义者，他将酒精描述为一种压迫工具，用来麻痹被奴役者的思想。

sentences.en: Those progressive causes happened to be the abolition of slavery, the feminist movement, and the larger temperance movement.
sentences.zh: 道格拉斯在1845年说：“如果我们能让世界清醒，就不会有奴隶制。”并进一步解释说，所有伟大的改革都是相辅相成的。

sentences.en: And these causes overlapped constantly throughout the 19th into the 20th century.
sentences.zh: 考虑到在这个时代，我们看到的女性形象往往只是摩登女郎式的点缀，

sentences.en: Frederick Douglass was a famous teetotaler, framing alcohol as a tool of oppression to dull the minds of enslaved people by their oppressors.
sentences.zh: 我非常惊讶地发现，禁酒的推动力与美国第一波妇女运动直接重叠。

sentences.en: If we could but make the world sober, we would have no slavery, Douglass said in 1845, going on to explain that all great reforms go together.
sentences.zh: 争取投票权的运动与废除酒精的运动完全捆绑在一起。

sentences.en: And given that we only ever really see women as flapper set dressing in this era,
sentences.zh: 乔亚认为，禁酒令的历史无法从女权主义历史中剥离出来。

sentences.en: I was very surprised at how the push to ban alcohol directly overlapped with the first wave of the American women's movement.
sentences.zh: 当大多数其他形式的权力对女性不可用时，女性在这一运动中找到了政治力量。

sentences.en: The drive for the vote was completely tied up with the drive to abolish liquor.
sentences.zh: 在禁酒令的两派中，各种政治倾向的女性都处于组织的最前沿。

sentences.en: Joya makes the case that the history of prohibition cannot be extracted from feminist history.
sentences.zh: 一位女性负责执行禁酒令，而另一位女性则是促成其废除的催化剂。

sentences.en: Women found political power in the movement when most other forms of power were unavailable to them.
sentences.zh: 我想，这是一个关于女性的故事。

sentences.en: On both sides of prohibition, women of all political persuasions are at the top of organizing.
sentences.zh: 那么，最初是什么吸引女性加入节制运动的呢？

sentences.en: A woman was in charge of enforcing prohibition and a woman was the catalyst for getting it repealed.
sentences.zh: 这是一个实用主义和安全的问题。

sentences.en: And I thought, this is a woman's story.
sentences.zh: 从历史上看，她们和她们的孩子是酗酒男性的受害者。

sentences.en: So what attracted women to the temperance movement in the first place?
sentences.zh: 19世纪的女性其实喝得不多，而男性却像喝水一样喝酒。

sentences.en: It was a matter of pragmatism and safety.
sentences.zh: 饮酒对美国家庭来说是一个巨大的问题，因为当时的水不安全。
